entries.name: Loen
entries.notes: Loen Kingdom — the lingua franca of the Northern Continent

entries.name: Feysac
entries.notes: Feysac Empire — derived from Ancient Feysac

entries.name: Intis
entries.notes: Intis Republic — derived from Ancient Feysac

entries.name: Balam (Dutan)
entries.notes: East and West Balam, Southern Continent — distinct origin from Ancient Feysac but structurally similar

entries.name: Highland
entries.notes: Mountain regions of the Northern Continent — various dialects

entries.name: Rorsted
entries.notes: Rorsted Archipelago — derived from Ancient Feysac

entries.name: Ancient Hermes
entries.notes: Created by the ancient sage Hermes in the Second Epoch, based on Jotun and Dragonese. Direct, powerful — but lacks concealment, making it dangerous for the unprotected. Used for sacrifice and prayer.

entries.name: Hermes
entries.notes: The improved, safer descendant of Ancient Hermes. Better concealment and protection. Essential knowledge for all Beyonders.

entries.name: Elvish
entries.notes: Ancient language of the elves. Every word is rich in meaning; sentences are very short. Can shake natural forces. Used for sacrifice, prayer, and spellcasting.

entries.name: Dragonese
entries.notes: Ancient language of dragons. Can shake natural forces. Used for sacrifice, prayer, and spellcasting.

entries.name: Jotun (Giant's)
entries.notes: Ancient language of giants. Can shake natural forces. Still in daily use in the City of Silver (Forsaken Land of the Gods). Basis of Ancient Feysac.

entries.name: Ancient Feysac
entries.notes: Common tongue of the Fourth Epoch and root of all modern Northern Continent languages. Derived from Jotun. Has minor mystical properties but cannot shake natural forces. Considered a mystical language due to its origin and ritual use.
